Q: What is the meaning of the 'estimate' field in GitHub Projects? A:

Important topic. Teams often treat estimate as a generic number while using it for different decision layers, which creates planning noise. In my projects, separating effort estimate, duration expectation, and priority signal worked best, and that is also why I built AI Task Breakdown in Plexo to keep those values explicit at generation time. https://plexo.work How does your team currently use estimate in sprint planning versus roadmap reporting?

Q: Azure Web App | Deployment Error - Framework-dependent is an invalid value for the "SelfContained" parameter of the "ProcessFrameworkReferences" A:

The issue is a combination of both a need to "upgrade" and a misconfiguration in either your project or pubxml files.

.net 8 expects your .csproj and .pubxml files to have a section: <SelfContained></SelfContained> with either a true or false value.

In earlier version of .net, the SelfContained value could, in fact, use Framework-dependent as the value. I suspect that you created your project using an earlier version of .net and have upgraded it to .net 8.

You can either manually change these values in both your .csproj and .pubxml files, or attempt to run the .NET Upgrade Assistant (Available as a VS extension here) to have it review your solution to check for any other incorrect configuration values or dependencies that haven't correctly been migrated to .net 8.

Note that as of VS2022 version 17.14.16 the extension has been deprecated and has been replaced by GitHub copilot app modernization chat agent. You can still access the legacy version in VS by heading to: Tools → Options → Projects and Solutions → Modernization → Enable legacy Upgrade Assistant.

Q: PostgreSQL trigger causing infinite recursion when updating same table - how to prevent trigger from firing recursively? A:

At least drop the function sync_product_from_summary() and the trigger. If you want to set the last_modified column, do it in the function update_product_metadata().
